review_candidates.title: Project Manager - Biomass Storage Projects
review_candidates.description: Tivano builds large-scale underground biomass-storage sites in Namibia. These storage sites store woody biomass from selective bush thinning, keeping the carbon contained in the biomass out of the atmosphere for the long term and thereby delivering durable carbon removal. We are looking for a practical, highly organised Project Manager to lead the day-to-day construction and operation of these sites. No previous carbon-removal experience is required: we are primarily looking for someone with strong experience in construction, earthworks, agriculture, mining, logistics or comparable field operations. Initially, you will manage two sites near Otjiwarongo and coordinate contractors, machinery operators, day workers, specialists, landowners and farmers. You will ensure that work progresses safely, efficiently, on schedule and with complete documentation. This role is designed to grow with Tivano: from direct responsibility for individual construction sites to leading a nationwide portfolio of biomass-storage projects and the teams delivering them. What you will do Plan and coordinate daily activities across two active biomass-storage construction sites near Otjiwarongo. Coordinate contractors, day workers, plant and machinery, operators, materials and site logistics, including maintenance, spare parts and external support when needed. Set clear priorities, assign responsibilities and follow up on execution; involve and delegate to qualified professionals whenever specialist input is required. Monitor progress, workmanship, deadlines and site readiness, identify bottlenecks early and resolve practical issues on the ground. Ensure that safety requirements are understood and followed, including site briefings, appropriate protective equipment and intervention when work is unsafe. Supervise the biomass weighing process, verify weighing records and supporting documentation, and maintain reliable daily site records and progress updates. Coordinate closely with landowners and farmers and maintain constructive working relationships with local stakeholders. How the role will grow Coordinate the smooth execution of a nationwide portfolio of up to ten projects, with consistent standards for planning, safety, quality, documentation and delivery. Manage, guide and develop several project managers or site leads, set priorities across projects, review progress and remove operational bottlenecks. Play a key role in hiring decisions, workforce and human-capital planning, onboarding, upskilling and the development of capable local teams. Negotiate and manage operational and commercial agreements with contractors, suppliers and other project partners. Assess and onboard new projects across Namibia, translating new opportunities into practical execution plans, suitable teams and launch-ready sites. What we are looking for Relevant experience in project management, site supervision or field operations - ideally in construction, earthworks, agriculture, forestry, logistics, mining or a similar hands-on environment. Practical and mechanically minded: comfortable around machinery, able to understand how work is actually carried out, and willing to step in when needed. Strong organisational skills and a calm, dependable and clear and confident working style, with the ability to coordinate several workstreams and lead diverse operational teams respectfully. Strong attention to safety, accurate documentation and operational detail, combined with sound judgement under pressure. The leadership potential to build, coach and manage project teams as the project portfolio grows. Commercial confidence and the ability to negotiate clear, workable agreements while maintaining constructive long-term relationships. Fluent English and Afrikaans is required and Oshiwambo, Otjiherero, or German proficiency is an additional plus. A valid driving licence and the right to work in Namibia. An established network among contractors, machinery providers or agricultural operators in Namibia and/or South Africa is an advantage. Practical details The role is based in Otjiwarongo and starts no later than 1 October 2026. This is a field-based, predominantly on-site role. Occasional weekend work may be required during critical construction phases. What we offer A key operational role in delivering some of Namibia's first large-scale biomass-storage projects. Substantial responsibility and the authority to improve how projects are organised and executed in a fast-moving international team. A clear path from managing individual construction sites to leading Tivano’s growing portfolio of projects and operational teams across Namibia and South Africa. A competitive salary, commensurate with relevant experience and the level of responsibility. How to apply Please submit your CV and a short note describing your relevant site or project experience, current location, availability and salary expectations to team@tivano-carbon.com. Tivano is committed to building a diverse operational team. We particularly encourage applications from women and candidates from backgrounds currently underrepresented in construction and field operations.
